name: Post-Employment Non-Compete Restriction
precedent: Percept D'Mark (India) v. Zaheer Khan (2006) 4 SCC 227
pattern: (shall not|will not|agrees not to)\s+(engage in|work for|consult with|compete with|enter into employment with)\s+(any competitor|any competing business|similar business).*?(for a period of|within)\s*(\d+|one|two|three|12|24|36)\s*(months|years|year)
description: Clause restrains an individual from practicing their profession or engaging in employment after contract termination. Under Section 27 Indian Contract Act and Supreme Court precedent, all post-termination non-compete clauses are void ab initio in India.
remedy: Replace with strict confidentiality protection (NDAs) and non-solicitation of active clients/trade secrets, rather than blanket prohibition on livelihood.

name: One-Sided Uncapped Indemnification
precedent: Gajanan Moreshwar Parelkar v. Moreshwar Madan Mantri (AIR 1942 Bom 302)
pattern: indemnify[\s,]+defend[\s,]+and hold harmless.*?(against any and all|all claims|all liabilities|losses|damages|attorneys'? fees)(?!.*?mutual|reciprocal)
description: Party imposes blanket obligation to indemnify without reciprocal obligation from counterparty and without liability cap or exclusion of consequential damages.
remedy: Make indemnity bilateral, cap liability at total contract value or fees paid in preceding 12 months, and explicitly carve out indirect/consequential damages.

name: Punitive Liquidated Damages / Penalty Clause
precedent: ONGC v. Saw Pipes Ltd. (2003) 5 SCC 705 & Kailash Nath Associates v. DDA (2015) 4 SCC 136
pattern: (liquidated damages|penalty|forfeit).*?(exceeding|sum of|percentage of).*?(shall be deemed fair|regardless of actual proof of loss|irrevocably forfeited)
description: Contracts stipulating unreasonable stipulated damages without relation to genuine pre-estimate of loss. Under Section 74, Indian courts grant only 'reasonable compensation' not exceeding the penalty.
remedy: Explicitly state that liquidated damages represent genuine pre-estimate of actual loss, and require proof of genuine injury where loss is quantifiable.

name: Unilateral Sole Arbitrator Appointment
statute: Section 12(5) & Seventh Schedule, Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
precedent: Perkins Eastman Architects DPC v. HSCC (India) Ltd. (2020) 20 SCC 760
pattern: (sole arbitrator|arbitrator)\s+(appointed exclusively by|nominated solely by|designated by the company|at the sole discretion of)
description: Clause grants one party exclusive unilateral authority to appoint the sole arbitrator. Invalidated by Supreme Court under Section 12(5) for lack of independence and impartiality.
remedy: Provide for mutual agreement on sole arbitrator within 30 days, failing which appointment through High Court under Section 11(6), or institutional arbitration (DIAC/MCIA).

name: Overbroad Assignment of Pre-Existing & Personal IP
precedent: Indian Performing Right Society Ltd. v. Eastern India Motion Pictures (1977) 2 SCC 820
pattern: (assigns and transfers|hereby assigns).*?(all inventions|any and all ideas|intellectual property).*?(whether or not related to|conceived at any time|outside working hours)
description: Attempts to capture inventions created outside working hours without company resources, or lacks automatic lapse provisions under Section 19(5) Copyright Act.
remedy: Limit IP assignment strictly to work product developed in direct scope of employment/contract, using company assets.

name: Asymmetrical Termination for Convenience
precedent: Central Inland Water Transport Corp v. Brojo Nath Ganguly (AIR 1986 SC 1571)
pattern: (company|client|employer)\s+may terminate.*?(at its sole convenience|without cause|immediately).*?(contractor|employee|service provider)\s+(shall not have the right|requires.*?(notice of\s*(\d+|60|90)\s*days))
description: One party can terminate instantly without cause, while the counterparty is locked into onerous notice periods or prohibited from exit. Unconscionable bargain under Indian jurisprudence.
remedy: Establish reciprocal notice periods (e.g. 30 days written notice) for termination for convenience.
